$comment: kit:generated -- the schema of kit.yml, from the kit package; see: "Changing what kit adds" in .kit/1st.md, to replace it
title: kit.yml
description: The repository's settings. The kit writes three keys in it, version, packages, and excludes, and reads the rest. kit adds this schema through its kit package; to change it, see "Changing what kit adds" in .kit/1st.md rather than editing it. Each key is described in https://github.com/empowerite/kit/blob/main/docs/packages.md. To have an editor validate the file against this schema, add the modeline: # yaml-language-server: $schema=.kit/kit.schema.json

forge.description: The forge (the service that hosts the repository) of the primary remote, which the workflow commands use: github, gitlab, or ado (Azure DevOps). When absent, it is detected from the primary's host: github.com, gitlab.com, dev.azure.com, or a host under visualstudio.com, or a host the gh or glab CLI has logged in to. Otherwise it must be set here, as for an Azure DevOps Server, or set to none for a primary on a host with no forge the kit knows, such as Bitbucket or a plain git server: then nothing is asked of a forge, and a change is not read.

anyOf.description: a provider the repository adds on its module path, bash_path

forges.description: The forge of each remote named, by remote: {upstream: gitlab}. A remote not named here takes the forge its host names, or none; none names a remote with no forge. For the primary, forge wins over this.

anyOf.description: a provider the repository adds on its module path, bash_path

forge_settings.description: Each forge's own settings, by forge, read only when that forge is the primary's: {ado: {type: Bug}}, and stand_ins for any forge.

stand_ins.description: Stand-ins for features the forge lacks, or that the repository marks its own way; each is used even where the forge has the feature.

drafts.description: A change is a draft while it has the label, or while its title starts with the prefix, which kit leaves off the title it judges; kit ready takes either off.

closing-issues.description: The issues a change closes are the forge's own its body names with a closing keyword: Closes #7.

marks.description: The forge's stages are stale every so many seconds, 10 at the least, for a forge without cheap marks.

ado.description: Azure DevOps: how the forge's own tracker, Azure Boards, opens and closes a work item.

type.description: The type of a new work item. Default: Task.

closed_state.description: The state a work item closed as completed is set to. Default: Closed.

removed_state.description: The state a work item closed as not planned or a duplicate is set to. Default: Removed.

stand_ins.description: Stand-ins for features the forge lacks, or that the repository marks its own way; each is used even where the forge has the feature.

drafts.description: A change is a draft while it has the label, or while its title starts with the prefix, which kit leaves off the title it judges; kit ready takes either off.

closing-issues.description: The issues a change closes are the forge's own its body names with a closing keyword: Closes #7.

marks.description: The forge's stages are stale every so many seconds, 10 at the least, for a forge without cheap marks.

primary.description: The primary remote. Ahead and behind, the default branch, pull requests, builds, releases, and issues are read from it. Default: origin.

gate.description: The command kit gate runs. When absent, kit gate detects a root justfile ci recipe, a Makefile ci target, or a package.json ci script.

require_signing.description: When true, kit commit, kit work's start commit, and kit rebase sign every commit they make, and refuse before writing anything when git has no signing key configured; kit release signs its tag.

log_days.description: How many days kit keeps its logs under .kit/logs/: kit-YYYY-MMDD.log, a line per kit call, and mcp-YYYY-MMDD.log, a line per kit serve request. A day's first line removes each log last written more than this many days before. 0 writes no logs.

facts.description: What kit facts hands a policy engine beyond names.

read.description: Globs of the files whose content kit facts gives as text in the tree, so a rule can judge what a file says. A binary file, or one over 65536 bytes, has no text, and kit warns. A glob that matches nothing is ignored.

linked_exempt.description: Logins whose changes kit linked passes without a linked issue, and kit policy passes without checking the branch, the commit subjects, the pull request title, or the tree, each saying so by name: a bot such as dependabot[bot], whose changes have no issue and never will. One login per line under the key.

^[a-z_]+$.description: The value a package's templates use for this key, written @key@ in a template.

trackers.description: The issue trackers the workflow uses in addition to the forge's own issues. The forge's tracker handles the # prefix unless an entry here claims it. A reference names its tracker by its prefix: #7, AB#4521.

prefix.description: The text a reference to this tracker starts with, before the number: AB# for Azure DevOps work items.

provider.description: The tracker that handles the prefix: forge for the forge's own issues, ado for Azure DevOps work items, web for a ticket system kit reaches through its pages alone.

anyOf.description: a provider the repository adds on its module path, bash_path

project.description: ado: the project a new work item is created in.

type.description: ado: the type of a new work item. Default: Task.

closed_state.description: ado: the state kit close --completed sets. Default: Closed.

removed_state.description: ado: the state a work item closed as not planned or a duplicate is set to. Default: Removed.

new.description: web: the page a person files a new issue at; {title} in it stands for the title, encoded for a URL.

url.description: web: an issue's page; {id} in it stands for the issue's number.

policy.description: The patterns that the branch name, commit subjects, and the open change's title must match. Each is an extended regular expression, limited to the subset RE2 also supports. An absent key uses the kit's default. An empty pattern turns that rule off.

branch.description: The pattern for the branch name. Default: ^[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, the shape kit work gives a branch.

commit_subject.description: The pattern for the subject of every commit since the branch forked. Default: ^([A-Z]+)?#[0-9]+ [^ ], a subject that starts with its issue's reference.

change_title.description: The pattern for the open change's title, a pull request on GitHub or a merge request on GitLab. Default: ^[^[:cntrl:]]{1,120}$.

policy_engine.description: The policy engine: patterns, matched in bash, or opa, which evaluates the Rego under .kit/policy. When absent, opa is used if a .rego file is there, and patterns otherwise.

anyOf.description: a provider the repository adds on its module path, bash_path

bash_path.description: The bash module path: the directories that `use <module>` sources every <module>.sh from, in order, so a later directory overrides or extends an earlier one. It starts with kit:modules/bash/, the kit's own modules. An entry is kit:<dir>, a directory in the installed kit; an absolute directory; ~/<dir>, in the home directory; or a directory relative to the repository root. A directory that does not exist is skipped, as PATH skips one. Default: [kit:modules/bash/].

flow.description: The stages kit flow draws, in order: backlog, underway, desk, worktrees, changes, builds, incoming, releases. A stage left out is not drawn, but kit flow <stage> still prints it. Default: all eight, in that order.

version.description: The kit release the repository runs and is installed at: bin/kit, the loader, reads this line alone, so it is a plain version on one line. kit install and kit update write it; kit --version=<release> update moves it. A checkout of the kit itself declares unreleased.

packages.description: The active packages, in dependency order, written by kit install, kit update, and kit package.

excludes.description: Members of an active bundle removed with kit packages remove, which kit update leaves out.

sources.description: Sources of packages beyond the kit's release, in order; a later one's package replaces a package of the same name. Each is a tarball pinned by the sha256 digest of its bytes. See docs/packages.md.

name.description: The source's name, which kit packages shows and a bash_path entry <name>:<dir> uses.

url.description: git:<owner>/<repo>@<tag>, the forge's tarball of that tag, or a URL curl fetches.

digest.description: The sha256 digest of the tarball's bytes; a source with any other is refused.

tools.description: The tools the kit toolchain pins, by name: each a version and the url of its download, which tools.lock records for every platform. See docs/toolchains/using-kit.md.

version.description: The exact version, quoted so YAML keeps it as written: "1.20", not 1.2.

url.description: The download, with {version}, {platform}, {os}, and {arch} filled in.

bin.description: The directory, in what the url unpacks to, that holds the tool's commands; . by default.

profile.description: Install it on a desk alone, or on a runner alone; both when absent.

os.description: The tool's names for kit's linux and macos, as {macos: darwin}.

arch.description: The tool's names for kit's x64 and arm64, as {x64: amd64}.

platforms.description: The platforms it is locked for; all four when absent.
